root_cause: applyInboundRumor's upsert matched the FIRST row of the (messageId, reactor, emoji) triple including tombstones and returned null when it was removed ('removal wins regardless of arrival order'), with no notion of time. A re-add therefore never revived a tombstone for peers; for the sender the optimistic re-add was a separate live row (applyOptimistic inserts by id), and its echo matched the older tombstone and was discarded, so it never got an eventId. Round 1: round-0's tombstone-revive still lost removals that arrived with no live row to apply to, and confirming a live row ignored time, so 9 of 24 arrival orders of add@5 remove@10 add@11 remove@12 ended wrong and a stale echo could take over a pending re-add.
fix: Last-writer-wins register per (messageId, reactor, emoji) triple, one row each: createdAt = newest add, removedAt = newest removal (max-folded); live iff the add second is strictly later than the removal, tie => removed; legacy tombstones (no removedAt) keep removal-wins. Every emoji-tagged inbound removal is remembered (hidden removal-only tombstone when no row exists, never rendered or counted). Inbound adds only raise times, and take eventId only for the id-matching optimistic row or a not-older add on a non-removed row. applyOptimistic merges into the existing triple row; rollback of a merged re-add returns it to the tombstone. Untagged removals unchanged (not remembered, documented). Group (ChatStoreContext) and DM (ContactChat) share these functions; no caller changes. Round 2 (re-review findings): applyOptimistic appends beside a legacy tombstone and is a no-op on an already-live row (so a failed send cannot delete or tombstone a confirmed reaction); a tagged removal that leaves the row live keeps the pending re-add eventId; 4 regression tests incl. the removal-failure restore path.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The round-0 report framed the bug as 'revive a tombstone', but correctness needs an order-independent model; only a generated all-permutations test (which I had skipped for a few hand-picked orders) exposes such gaps. The sender's optimistic row plus its older echo made the single-row-per-triple rule necessary.
retrospective.surprised_by: Mixed resolution (optimistic ms vs rumor seconds) forced comparing at second resolution and bumping a local re-add past the removal's second.
